subject: Hosted API pricing & procurement questions — Poseidon Health
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Ellen Brooks <ellen.brooks@poseidonhealth.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-04T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Redwood hosted API pricing & next steps

Hi Ellen —

Great speaking this morning. Per our demo, I attached the pricing tiers that map to your expected monthly token volumes and the simple commit options we discussed. The short version: hosted API is usage-based per token, and we offer step discounts at commit tiers (monthly committed spend buckets) plus an overage rate that is lower than retail.

Key points you asked about:
- Volume discounts: material at 1M+ monthly tokens and deeper at 5M+; see "pricing_matrix_v2.xlsx" for example stacks.
- Commit tiers: you can select a monthly commit (USD) for a 12-month term; committing gives you an effective per-token discount and predictable budget.
- PO & vendor form: we can accept standard POs and we have a preferred vendor form — I attached our instructions to simplify procurement.

Next steps: if you can share the PO terms or the vendor form they need completed, I’ll loop in legal and finance. Dev is cc’d for anything technical (rate limits, burst capacity, dedicated routing).

Thanks —
Marissa
Marissa Cole | Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0198
https://redwood.com

Attachments: Redwood_Pricing_Tiers_Q2.pdf, pricing_matrix_v2.xlsx, Preferred_Vendor_Form_PO_instructions.pdf

From: Ellen Brooks <ellen.brooks@poseidonhealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-05T08:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood hosted API pricing & next steps

Marissa —

Thanks for the materials. Procurement reviewed and we have two blockers before we can put a PO through: 1) we need Redwood to complete our preferred vendor form (attached) and 2) we require unit pricing to be fixed for the length of the PO or a clear CPI-linked escalation clause — our finance team avoids purely variable pricing on critical vendor spend.

Also, your pricing spreadsheet shows commit tiers denominated in dollars; can you translate the example tiers into a guaranteed per-token floor price with the committed monthly spend(s)? We’re trying to model three scenarios for our budget: conservative (2M tokens/mo), expected (6M tokens/mo), and peak (15M tokens/mo).

If you prefer, we can share our vendor form and PO template (I attached our standard).

Appreciate a quick turnaround — our SOW timeline targets signing before the end of March.

Best,
Ellen Brooks
Sr. Procurement Manager, Poseidon Health
ellen.brooks@poseidonhealth.com

Attachments: Poseidon_Vendor_Form.pdf, PO_Template_PO-2026.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Ellen Brooks <ellen.brooks@poseidonhealth.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-05T11:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood hosted API pricing & next steps

Hi Ellen —

Thanks — we can complete your vendor form. I’ve looped in Grace from legal to help with terms and Dev to confirm technical SLOs. Quick answers up front:

1) Fixed unit pricing vs. usage-based: We typically sell hosted API as usage-based with commit tiers. For a 12-month commit you can select a guaranteed effective per-token price for the committed volume; overages bill at the agreed overage rate. That gives you a fixed-known cost for committed buckets and the ability to scale beyond with predictable overage pricing.

2) I converted the three scenarios to illustrative per-token floors in the attached "Redwood_Pricing_Tiers_Q2.pdf". Summary (examples):
- Conservative (2M/mo): commit $4,000/mo -> effective floor $0.0020 per token
- Expected (6M/mo): commit $9,500/mo -> effective floor $0.00158 per token
- Peak (15M/mo): commit $20,000/mo -> effective floor $0.00133 per token

These are example structures — final floors depend on model mix, average tokens per call, and whether you want a higher reserved throughput SLA. If PO requires fixed unit rates rather than commit+overage, we can provide a fixed per-token price for the PO term but that generally needs a higher effective rate to offset capacity risk.

Action items: If you send the vendor form, Grace will complete the legal sections and I’ll return a filled copy within 2 business days. Dev — can you confirm our burst support and sustained QPS for the 15M scenario so we can include an appendix?

Thanks,
Marissa

From: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ellen Brooks <ellen.brooks@poseidonhealth.com>
Date: 2026-03-06T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood hosted API pricing & next steps

Ellen / Marissa —

Confirming technical details for the 15M tokens/mo scenario:
- Sustained throughput: we recommend reserving Dedicated burst capacity for predictable latencies at that scale; hosted can sustain 15M tokens with a mixed-model approach (auto-batching + prefix caching).
- Typical observed latency: 95th percentile ~180-250ms per request for short context; will vary by model.
- Rate limits: we can set customer-level QPS policies and support scheduled bursts; if you need sub-100ms SLAs we should discuss Dedicated or Reserved pools.

I’ll add a short appendix to the vendor form describing our throttling and fallback behavior.

—Dev

From: Ellen Brooks <ellen.brooks@poseidonhealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-09T13:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood hosted API pricing & next steps

Marissa —

We reviewed the updated PDFs. Procurement prefers a single line-item in the PO with a fixed unit price and a not-to-exceed (NTE) annual cap. They will not accept commit+overage without a fixed per-token rate on the PO. Is Redwood willing to accept a fixed per-token price for the PO term with quarterly reconciliation against actual usage and either a true-up or credit? If so, what would the fixed per-token price be for the expected 6M tokens/mo scenario and what NTE annual cap would you recommend?

Also, the finance team is insisting on Net 60 payment terms and a limited set of invoice descriptors (PO #, invoice date, purchase description). Can you confirm Redwood’s flexibility on Net 60 and the invoice format?

Thanks,
Ellen

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Ellen Brooks <ellen.brooks@poseidonhealth.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-10T16:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood hosted API pricing & next steps

Ellen —

Appreciate the clarity. Short answers: yes, we can do a fixed per-token line on the PO with quarterly reconciliation and true-up/credit; and we can accommodate Net 60 on an enterprise agreement (finance will need to run a quick credit check). High-level proposal for the expected 6M/mo profile:

- Fixed per-token PO price (12-month term): $0.00165 per token (reflects a small premium to commit pricing to cover capacity risk).
- Recommended NTE annual cap: set to 12 * (6,000,000 tokens * $0.00165) = $118,800. We suggest a 10% headroom for unexpected spikes -> NTE $130,680.
- Quarterly reconciliation: if actuals are below committed equivalents we will issue a credit; if above, overage is billed at the agreed overage rate per the PO at the time of reconciliation. Grace will include language for reconciliation and audit rights.

We’ll complete your vendor form and return it with the PO line item language. Grace — can you confirm acceptable language for Net 60 and invoicing descriptors? Finance will start the credit check once you confirm PO value and billing cadence.

If that sounds OK I can produce a draft PO line and a one-page commercial summary for your CFO. Can we target signoff by March 24 so we can schedule onboarding for April?

Best,
Marissa

Attachments: Redwood_Pricing_Tiers_Q2.pdf (updated)
